claim: SEG transforms scattered evidence into a unified, temporal, contradiction-aware knowledge graph where every claim, source, derivation, and agent becomes a node, and every relationship (supports, contradicts, derives, witnesses) becomes an edge.

SEG provides four core guarantees: complete provenance (every claim traces to source), temporal awareness (bitemporal storage enables 'what was known at time T?' queries), contradiction detection (automatic detection of conflicting claims), and auditable knowledge (JSON-LD export, RDF serialization, SHACL validation).

SEG synthesizes knowledge from multiple sources (VIF witnesses, APOE plans, documents), detects contradictions before they cause problems, traces lineage ('where did this claim come from?'), queries temporal snapshots ('what was true on 2025-02-01?'), and exports evidence graphs for external analysis tools.

SEG graph schema includes node types (Claim, Source, Derivation, Agent), edge types (supports, contradicts, derives, witnesses, cites), and bitemporal fields (Transaction time when recorded, Valid time when true).

SEG contradiction detector uses semantic similarity (embedding-based) for finding similar claims and stance detection (positive/negative/neutral) for conflict analysis, automatically creating 'contradicts' edges and flagging conflicts.

SEG query engine supports lineage tracing (backward: find sources, forward: find derivations), temporal queries (what was true at time T?), provenance chains (complete source-to-claim paths), and contradiction queries (what conflicts with claim X?).
SEG export system provides JSON-LD (W3C standard, RDF-compatible), RDF serialization (triple store compatible), and SHACL validation (shape validation for graph integrity) for external tools.

SEG integrates with VIF (witnesses link claims), APOE (plans record evidence), CMC (stores graph nodes/edges), HHNI (retrieves context for synthesis), and SDF-CVF (ensures quartet parity for evidence artifacts).
SEG consists of four core components: Graph Builder, Contradiction Detector, Conflict Resolver, and Knowledge Synthesizer.

SEG uses graph-first design (evidence as nodes/edges), bitemporal foundation (transaction time + valid time), provenance discipline (every claim must have source), automatic contradiction detection (semantic similarity + stance analysis), and standards compliance (JSON-LD, RDF, SHACL).

SEG real-world workflows include evidence validation pipeline (coverage check, contradiction detection, knowledge synthesis), contradiction resolution (retrieve details, weight evidence, resolve with provenance), and temporal evidence queries (snapshot reconstruction, historical analysis).

SEG operational runbook includes weekly evidence audit (sample claims, verify anchors, check freshness, detect contradictions, record results), release checklist (coverage query, contradiction query, block on failures), and change logging (all changes logged with reviewer, timestamp, reason).

SEG performance characteristics: graph operations (node creation ~10ms, edge creation ~5ms, contradiction detection ~100ms per pair, synthesis ~500ms per topic), query performance (coverage ~50ms, contradictions ~200ms, temporal ~100ms, lineage ~30ms).

SEG contradiction types include direct contradictions (opposite claims about same topic), temporal contradictions (claims true at different times), and contextual contradictions (claims true in different contexts).

SEG resolution workflow: SEG raises review task with full context, authors investigate both claims, authors reconcile (update claim, mark resolved, add context), resolution recorded in SEG with provenance, contradiction edge removed or marked resolved.
